{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Mobile app", "POST /premium/unlock endpoint", "Entitlement service", "Account/premium flag store"],
    "dataStores": ["Account entitlement records"],
    "externalServices": ["App Store / Play Store purchase receipts"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Mobile client to backend API", "Backend to app store receipt verification"],
    "dataClasses": ["payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false,
    "dataFlows": []
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Anyone can send purchased=true and get premium without paying",
      "scenario": "An attacker with the mobile app intercepts or hand-crafts a request to POST /premium/unlock with the body flag set to purchased true and no valid purchase. Because the backend makes the entitlement decision from a client-supplied field, every user can self-grant premium features for free, at scale, and the loss is unbounded revenue plus free access to paid functionality.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-602", "CWE-807"],
      "plainLanguage": "The app tells the server 'I paid' and the server believes it, so anyone can unlock premium for free.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Server decides entitlement from a verified receipt, never from a client flag",
        "given": "a client calls POST /premium/unlock",
        "when": "the request body contains a purchased flag or any other client-asserted entitlement value",
        "then": "the server ignores that value and grants premium only after it has itself verified the receipt with the App Store or Play Store verification API and confirmed the product, status and transaction are valid"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Forged or edited store receipts are never checked with Apple or Google",
      "scenario": "A user edits the receipt blob sent to POST /premium/unlock, or supplies a receipt generated by a jailbroken device or a fake store proxy. The design describes no server-side verification call to the store, so a tampered receipt is accepted and premium is unlocked. This also makes sandbox or test receipts usable against production accounts.",
      "component": "Receipt handling in /premium/unlock",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-345", "CWE-20"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nobody asks Apple or Google whether the receipt is real, so a fake one works.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Verify every receipt server-to-server against the store",
        "given": "a receipt is submitted to the unlock endpoint",
        "when": "the server processes it",
        "then": "the server validates it over a server-to-server call to the store's verification endpoint, rejects sandbox receipts in production, and rejects the request if validation fails or is unavailable rather than unlocking premium"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "One real receipt replayed on many accounts",
      "scenario": "A paying attacker captures their own genuine receipt and posts it to POST /premium/unlock from many different accounts, or sells it on. With no record binding a transaction id to a single account and no single-use check, one purchase unlocks premium for an unlimited number of accounts.",
      "component": "Entitlement service",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-294", "CWE-837"],
      "plainLanguage": "One person buys premium once and the same receipt can be reused to unlock it for everyone else.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Bind each store transaction to exactly one account, once",
        "given": "a receipt with a store transaction id has already been redeemed",
        "when": "the same transaction id is submitted again, by any account",
        "then": "the server rejects the request, does not change any entitlement, and records the duplicate redemption attempt against both accounts"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Unlock applied to an account chosen by the caller",
      "scenario": "The design says premium is unlocked 'for the account' but does not say the account is taken from the authenticated session. If the unlock request carries an account or user identifier, an attacker can change it to unlock, downgrade or churn another customer's entitlement, or map their own receipt onto an account they do not own.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the request says which account to upgrade, someone could point it at a stranger's account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Derive the target account from the session, not the request",
        "given": "an authenticated call to POST /premium/unlock",
        "when": "the body or query contains an account, user or device identifier",
        "then": "the server ignores it and applies the entitlement only to the account bound to the authenticated session"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Unlock endpoint has no stated authentication",
      "scenario": "The recorded signals show no authentication for this work item, and the design describes the endpoint only as a call the app makes. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach POST /premium/unlock can drive entitlement changes directly against the backend without ever holding an account credential, bypassing the app entirely.",
      "component": "POST /premium/unlock endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "When a purchase succeeds the app calls POST /premium/unlock with the receipt." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing in the design says you have to be logged in to call the unlock endpoint.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require an authenticated session on the unlock endpoint",
        "given": "a request to POST /premium/unlock",
        "when": "it carries no valid user session or token",
        "then": "the server returns 401, performs no entitlement change, and the mobile client is the only path that can obtain such a session"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No link between an entitlement and the purchase that justified it",
      "scenario": "Because the unlock decision is made from a client flag, nothing durable records which store transaction granted premium to which account. Support and finance cannot tell a genuine purchase from a self-granted one, cannot process refunds or revoke entitlement when the store reports a cancellation or chargeback, and a user can deny or claim a purchase with no way to settle the dispute.",
      "component": "Account entitlement records",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The server trusts the client flag \"purchased\": true and unlocks premium for the account." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "The system cannot show why an account has premium, so refunds, chargebacks and fraud cannot be sorted out.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Store the verified transaction behind every entitlement and honour store revocations",
        "given": "premium is granted to an account",
        "when": "the grant is written",
        "then": "the store transaction id, product id, verification response and timestamp are stored with it, and a store refund, cancellation or chargeback notification revokes the entitlement automatically"
      }
    }
  ]
}
